> **Note:** This panel currently can't be opened from the on-screen panel list - its menu entry is commented out in firmware. The Wi-Li-nux folder now lists **Linux Terminal** instead, which talks to the CM0 Linux shell.

## Terminal

A text console into the device: type a line, press enter, and see the
response. This page covers two screens that share the same log-and-prompt
layout - the plain Terminal screen below, and the Linux Terminal screen,
which talks to a real shell on the CM0 Linux processor and has its own,
different button-bar behavior.

### The screen

A scrolling log fills most of the screen, oldest at the top and newest at
the bottom. Below it, a ">" prompt marks a text entry field where whatever
you type appears before you send it. The two screens keep separate logs.

### Terminal

| Button | Action |
|---|---|
| Cancel | This help page |

None of Gray, Yellow, Green, Blue or Red do anything on this screen. Text is
entered with the device's on-screen or attached keyboard input, not the
button bar.

### Typing a command

Type into the field after the ">" prompt and submit it to send the line to
the device's command interpreter - the same one the console understands over
USB. The field then clears itself and is ready for the next line. Anything
the interpreter prints back appears in the scrolling log above.

### Linux Terminal

Reached from the main menu's Wi-Li-nux folder. A submitted line goes
straight to a bash shell running on the CM0 Linux processor, not to the
device's own command interpreter, and whatever the shell prints back
appears in the scrolling log.

| Button | Action |
|---|---|
| Up | Recall an older command |
| Down | Recall a newer command |
| Center | Send the recalled command as-is |
| Green | Open an editor pre-filled with the recalled command, to change it before sending |
| Blue | Clear the log |
| Red | Ctrl-C |
| Cancel | Nothing - see "No way back" below |

### Recalling a command

Up and Down step through your last 8 submitted commands, newest first, and
preview whichever one you land on the prompt line; stepping past the oldest
or back past the newest just stops instead of wrapping. Center sends that
preview as-is. Green instead opens the on-screen keyboard with the preview
already typed in, so you can change it before sending. Submitting a line,
whether from the keyboard or from Green's editor, adds it to the history and
clears the preview.

This recall behavior is specific to the Linux Terminal. The plain Terminal
screen above keeps its inline keyboard armed at all times, which already
claims the colored buttons for typing, so it has no room for Up, Down or
Center to do anything else.

### Ctrl-C

Red sends a real Ctrl-C to the shell - useful for interrupting whatever is
currently running - without adding a newline or touching what's on the
prompt line. Its label reads "Ctrl-C" whenever the screen is idle. Green's
editor takes over all five button labels for its own keyboard while it is
open; earlier firmware left Red showing a home icon after the editor
closed instead of putting its own label back, so Red looked like an exit
button while it was still sending Ctrl-C underneath. That's fixed - closing
the editor now restores Red's real label.

### No way back

Neither screen returns you to the main menu on its own. The Linux Terminal
in particular does not give Red that job either - Red sends Ctrl-C, Green
opens the send editor, and Blue only clears the log. HOME is the only way
out of either screen, the same as it is everywhere else in the menu.

The Linux Terminal also has no help page of its own, so pressing Cancel
there does nothing - this page is reachable only from the main menu, through
the plain Terminal screen's Skelltris, Wili8 or Doom entries (see below),
not from the Linux Terminal screen itself.

### Reached from more than one menu entry

The main menu's Skelltris, Wili8 and Doom entries currently all open this
same Terminal screen too, as placeholders for those games.
